A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of the R-HDS regimen are similar to those of the R-CHOD-14 regimen, but R-CHOD is less toxic.
the R-CHP regimen is superior to the R-HDS regimen for the treatment of high-risk DLBCL.
R-HDS with ASCT did improve disease-free survival, but this was not translated into a significant improvement of overall survival because of late-occurrence of treatment-related deaths.
The main takeaway from our work is that
R-CHOP is the standard of care for the treatment of high-risk diffuse large B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and that high-dose sequential therapy with ASCT should be reserved for selected cases.
the R-CHOPS approach is an effective first-line treatment option for high-intermediate and high-risk patients with DLBCL.
the R-CHP regimen, with the same number of cycles as R-CHOP-14, should be used in the upfront treatment of patients with high-risk DLBCL.
